text: For the choirmaster. A maskil of David.
When Doeg the Edomite came to Saul and reported to him, saying, "David has gone to the house of Ahimelech."

versions.text: When Doeg the Edomite came and told Saul, "David has gone to the house of Ahimelech."
versions.explanation: The current wording is a sentence fragment and drops the Hebrew's 'and said to him'; adding 'saying' completes the introduction to the quotation and reads more smoothly aloud.

text: Why do you boast of evil, you mighty man? The mercy of God endures all day long.
Your tongue plots destruction, like a sharpened razor, you worker of deceit.
You love evil more than good, and lying more than speaking what is right. Selah
You love every devouring word, you deceitful tongue.
But God will tear you down forever; he will snatch you up and pull you from your tent, and uproot you from the land of the living. Selah
The righteous will see and stand in awe, and they will laugh at him:

versions.text: The righteous will see and be afraid, and they will laugh at him:
versions.explanation: The wordplay (see/fear) describes reverent awe at God's judgment rather than terror; 'be afraid' beside 'laugh at him' reads oddly for oral delivery.

text: "Look at the man who would not make God his refuge, but trusted in his great wealth and grew strong in his own wickedness."

versions.text: "Look at the man who would not make God his refuge, but trusted in his great wealth and grew strong through his destruction."
versions.explanation: הַוָּה here denotes the man's own wicked scheming/greed (the same root rendered 'destruction' in v.4), not something done to him. 'Through his destruction' is ambiguous in English and could be misread as God destroying him. 'In his own wickedness' preserves the sense and the parallel with his boasting.

text: But I am like a green olive tree in the house of God; I trust in God's mercy forever and ever.
I will praise you forever, because you have acted; and in the presence of your faithful I will hope in your name, for it is good.
